1.explanation:
1. Select.js defines the component’s class names, props (invalid/invalidText), and conditionally renders the error icon/text. This file must be extended to accept and render a warning prop (e.g. warning/warningText), add new ‘--select--warning’ CSS class, use the yellow WarningFilled16 icon, and apply the correct spacing.
2. Select-story.js contains the Storybook example and knobs; it needs to expose the new warning state in the UI and docs so designers can preview the style.
3. Select-test.js includes unit tests for rendering error/invalid; it must be updated to cover the new warning prop, verify the correct class, icon, and warning text are rendered when warning is true.
1.bug_scenario: The user wants to add a “warning” state to the React Select component—similar to the existing invalid/error state, but using a yellow warning icon and warning text, with specific spacing and color tokens. The supplied designs show: 16 px yellow-triangle icon (support-03 fill) to the right of the dropdown label, 16 px from the right edge, 8 px from the down-caret, and the warning message text below the control. Currently, passing invalid/invalidText only triggers the red error state with the built-in WarningFilled16 icon and “--select--invalid” styling, so a separate warning variant is needed.
